pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered as kettlebell work three to four times a week for 30-45 minutes plus a daily mobility programme built around his hips. He engaged with the mechanics rather than just accepting: 'I just want, because I'm looking, I don't know what's the result I can have in terms of body, because it's from two to three sessions per week, right?' He then corrected himself upward — 'two, I was like, in my opinion, it's not too little, so I was surprised' — and volunteered the delivery constraint that matters to him: 'I need to have in my calendar, every like Monday X, every Wednesday X.' The rep confirmed three to four. Genuine understanding-seeking, no pushback on substance.

Presented as when-you-eat, what-you-eat, how-much-you-eat with light time restriction and mainly whole foods. He accepted it directly — 'Yes, I'll just manage time and that's it' — and ranked it highly unprompted afterwards: 'the food is very important, actually, I think.' He did push back once on a mechanism, citing a friend's claim that entrepreneurs need to eat in the morning because of stress, and accepted the rep's correction without argument. He had already pre-qualified himself on this pillar earlier: 'if I have a plan, if I have a good plan, I know I'll follow it.'

This is the pillar he came for and he tied it to his own diagnosis repeatedly and without prompting: 'having a coach that is behind you', 'Because I'll have somebody that is pushing me. Like when I had the boxing sessions, I had no choice', and 'even though let's say it's not even a matter of knowledge... the fact of having someone behind you has a huge consequence on the result.' When asked what spoke most to him he said 'I think the three things. I mean, the program, someone behind, and then the food.' The only friction was mechanical — he asked whether the community was on WhatsApp or Skool, whether there were Zoom sessions, and which app was used — and one substantive gap: the written material the rep sent omitted the one-to-one entirely, which the prospect immediately spotted ('Yeah, this is not the one-to-one thing') and which the rep conceded is 'like the biggest part'.

anchors.raw: Because I just did the calculations, but in six months, it's a bit actually pricey. What I think is like, it's almost 900. I did in the US, it's almost 900 per month. And I think it's a bit pricey.
anchors.note: He converted the lump sum into a monthly rate himself, unprompted, and only then found it expensive — the $6,000 figure drew no reaction at all when first stated ('Yeah. For how long is it?'). The lump-sum framing was holding; the per-month framing broke it. Worth knowing that a self-generated monthly number is what created price resistance in an otherwise price-insensitive buyer.

anchors.raw: even if the price is a bit pricey in my opinion because uh but if you go for personal trainer in the gym you're going to be
anchors.note: He supplied the justification for the price himself before the rep could, cutting off mid-sentence as the rep took it over ('But they're not there to give you an actual transformation'). He has genuine reference pricing here: he previously paid a boxing coach to come to his home twice a week.

anchors.raw: Maybe I could, I don't know, you, how much you guys make, honestly. Maybe you make more, maybe you make less than us. I don't know. It's not a competition. But now we have a process where we do it in a two times closing. Because our products is more expensive than you guys.
anchors.note: The strongest supportive anchor in the call: he sells higher-ticket digital products himself, employs closers, and said twice that he was not debating price ('I'm not even debating the price. I'm just debating that. You want a fact check.'). Price was never the obstacle. It also makes his procedural objection more, not less, credible — he is describing how his own company sells at this price point.

anchors.raw: what I like is that it's not only sport, there's intuition, there's more features than that. So that's why I'm willing to pay
anchors.note: The nutrition pillar is what justified the price for him, over training. He volunteered this in the final two minutes, after the price objection had already been conceded.

unmet_demand.want: Anything written describing what the programme is, to read alone before committing — 'I want something written where it says, what's the plan' and 'I want to always want to take the time to read it calmly and alone'.
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No such asset exists. The rep said 'we don't have anything that we send to people', 'this is the only thing that we've written down', and 'I couldn't find anything more new'. What he did send was an old internal document that he immediately had to disclaim as omitting the one-to-one coaching — the primary deliverable — which the prospect spotted himself.

unmet_demand.want: Sight of the agreement before paying — 'you send me the contract, I read, if it's, if there is one' and 'the contract, you sent it before and after, right?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The agreement is generated automatically only after payment and the rep has no pre-payment access to it: 'I don't have a site into the contract, it gets sent when we've done the payment' and 'I can't just open a new one, like, it's all automatic.' The prospect flagged this as a European norm mismatch — 'you cannot pay an after-signed contract. It doesn't work like this' — and the rep agreed it differs ('in Europe, it's a little bit different').

unmet_demand.want: Some evidence-based indication of what six months would actually produce for him — 'I always wonder what's going to be my body like in six months... can you tell?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep declined to forecast ('I cannot tell you') and substituted volume claims — 1,200 clients coached, 1.3 million followers — with no case study, before-and-after, or comparable client offered at any point in a 63-minute call.

unmet_demand.want: Live video contact with the coach beyond onboarding — 'is there Zoom sessions or just WhatsApp, right?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Deliberately not offered: 'It is overall always WhatsApp because when people are moving the whole time, we work with a lot of business. It's just a headache to get Zoom meetings booked in.' Beyond the single onboarding call and the weekly group live workout, one-to-one contact is text only.

unmet_demand.want: A stated refund or cancellation position — 'in worst case scenario in one week like I'm like totally disappointed... how does it work, can I get a refund?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no policy to quote. The rep improvised three different discretionary answers across the call ('we can go into conversation about that', 'if I've lied to you, then we would definitely give you a refund', 'if you're like, guys, I hate this, then we just send it back') and steered away from the question each time ('from what I'm hearing you're ready to commit... so it shouldn't be needed').
